acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass and producer Robyn Semien get a blackjack lesson from Andy Bloch, who played for the MIT blackjack team. He teaches them the basics of card-counting, the technique that gives players an advantage against the house — enough of an advantage that most casinos will ask you to leave if they catch you doing it.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Jack Hitt tells the story of the Christian card-counting team featured in the documentary Holy Rollers, and why they see no contradiction in being devout Christians who spend their days in casinos.
acts.title: Render Unto Caesar's Palace What Is Due To Caesar's Palace

acts.desc: Ira and Robyn go to the casino to try out their newfound card-counting skills.

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Producer Sarah Koenig tells the story of a woman who sued the casino where she lost her inheritance, saying that it was to blame, not her.
This story was inspired by a chapter in The Power of Habit, by Charles Duhigg.
